> a probe that times out or cannot reach the Graphite server keeps the lane
> rather than demoting, so a network blip never pushes a branch outside a real
> stack, and the verdict is cached between ships.

v0.39.0 inverted exactly that. An unanswerable probe now **demotes** — keeping a
lane nobody could confirm is what made the gate inert for four releases, since
every probe was timing out against a 5s cap and every timeout read as "keep".
The help text was the last place the old contract survived, so the binary was
documenting the bug as though it were the design.

It also claimed a flat "cached between ships", which was true when there were two
verdicts and is now three, each on its own span.

## The change

Two places, both saying what the code does: an unconfirmable lane declines, the
trade that makes that the safer half is named, and the three TTLs are spelled out
(a yes for a day, a no for an hour, an unanswered probe for a minute — so an
outage costs one probe a minute rather than one per command).

- `internal/cli/ship.go` — the long `--help` text.
- `plugin/skills/ccx/SKILL.md` — the shipped skill doc, which carried the same
  claim in shorter form. Hand-maintained, not a cc-guides artifact, so it needs
  fixing at the source rather than by re-rendering.

No behaviour change; this is documentation catching up to `baffb08`.

## Also

The same stale claim lived in `plugin/guides/md/ccx.md` over in cc-skills, which
renders into this repo's `AGENTS.md`. That landed separately as
`yasyf/cc-skills@f500d7d`, so the Guides bot will re-render `AGENTS.md` here on
its own.

## Verification

`go build ./...` clean. `ccx vcs ship --help` reads the corrected sentence. There
is no test to add — the string is the artifact.
